\[
K_{\phi}(x, y) = -\exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) - m_{\phi} \;\text{ for } |u| \le 3\sigma,\ |v| \le \tfrac{L}{2},\qquad R(p) = \max_{\phi} (K_{\phi} \star I)(p)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\phi\): The vessel direction
- \(u, v\): Offsets across and along the vessel
- \(L\): The length
- \(m_{\phi}\): The mean of the Gaussian part inside the window

For the vessel direction phi, u = x sin phi + y cos phi is the offset across the vessel and v = x cos phi - y sin phi the offset along it. The y axis points down, so phi turns counterclockwise on screen. The term m_phi is the mean of the Gaussian part over the offsets inside the window, so each kernel adds up to 0 and flat areas give 0. Offsets outside the window have weight 0. Bright vessels use the kernel with the opposite sign. The angle output is the direction of the largest response. When several are within 1e-9 times max(1, |R|) of it, the first wins. The choice of grid offsets inside the window is this filter's own discrete rule.
